sections.heading: Do I need a visa?
list: Citizens of some countries need a visa before they travel. Check with the official tool.
British citizens do not need a visa.
Some people with a UK visitor visa can visit without an Irish visa, under the British Irish Visa Scheme.
You can apply for a short stay 'C' visa up to 3 months before you travel.

sections.heading: At the airport or port
list: An immigration officer decides if you can come in. A visa lets you travel, but it does not promise entry.
Have your passport, your visa if you need one, and your boarding card ready.
It helps to bring your travel plans, proof of money, health insurance, where you are staying, and any invitation letters.
The officer puts a stamp in your passport. You can stay until the date on it, for 3 months at most.
Came in through Northern Ireland? Report to an immigration officer within 30 days, or within 7 days if you are here for work or business.

sections.heading: Staying longer than 3 months
list: You need permission to stay longer. A short stay 'C' visa means you must leave before your stamp ends.
With a long stay 'D' visa, register your permission before your landing stamp ends.

sections.heading: Lost or stolen passport
list: Report it to the Gardaí (Irish police).
Contact your country's embassy to get a replacement.
Tourist SOS can help you contact the Gardaí and your embassy.
